final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark remediation for VPC flow logging (reject traffic),
  implemented as custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks. The stack is fully
  self-contained and deployable unattended into a greenfield account with zero
  external dependencies: it creates the customer managed KMS key and the CloudWatch
  Logs log group that receive the flow log data, the VPC Flow Logs delivery role, the
  Automation execution role, a direct remediation runbook, and a Change Manager gated
  runbook together with the change template it uses. The target VPC is not a template
  input; it is supplied at run time as runbook input and the flow log is created
  against that VPC by the runbook.

Parameters:
  NamePrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: cis-vpc-flowlogs
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 32
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only (1-32 characters).'
    Description: >-
      Prefix used to name and tag every resource created by this template.

  ComplianceTag:
    Type: String
    Default: CIS-AWS-Foundations
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Letters, numbers, and the characters dot, underscore, colon and hyphen only (1-64 characters).'
    Description: >-
      Value applied to the Compliance tag of every taggable resource created by this
      template.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the compliance flow log data.
  # The key policy grants the regional CloudWatch Logs service principal in this
  # Region the encrypt/decrypt/generate data key permissions, restricted to the
  # log group created by this template through the aws:logs:arn encryption context.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  VpcFlowLogsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Customer managed KMS key that encrypts ${NamePrefix} VPC flow log data in CloudWatch Logs.'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableKeyAdministrationForAccount
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowCloudWatchLogsToEncryptFlowLogData
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: !Sub 'logs.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:ReEncryptFrom
              - kms:ReEncryptTo
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                'kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${NamePrefix}-vpc-flowlogs*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-vpc-flowlogs-key'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Destination log group for reject-traffic flow logs, retained with a
  # compliance-grade retention period so stack deletion cannot destroy evidence.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  VpcFlowLogsLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-vpc-flowlogs'
      RetentionInDays: 3653
      KmsKeyId: !GetAtt VpcFlowLogsKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-vpc-flowlogs'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Role assumed by the VPC Flow Logs delivery service to publish flow logs.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FlowLogDeliveryRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-flowlog-delivery-role'
      Description: >-
        Assumed by the VPC Flow Logs delivery service (delivery.logs.amazonaws.com)
        to publish reject-traffic flow logs into the CloudWatch Logs log group
        created by this template.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowVpcFlowLogsDeliveryServiceToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: delivery.logs.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${NamePrefix}-vpc-flowlogs:*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PublishFlowLogsToComplianceLogGroup
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteFlowLogEventsToLogGroup
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                Resource:
                  - !Sub '${VpcFlowLogsLogGroup.Arn}'
                  - !Sub '${VpcFlowLogsLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-flowlog-delivery-role'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Role assumed by SSM Automation while running the runbooks. It may manage flow
  # logs, pass only the flow log delivery role to the delivery service, and start
  # the automation / Change Manager change request created by this template.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AutomationExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-automation-exec-role'
      Description: >-
        Execution role assumed by AWS Systems Manager Automation while running the
        CIS VPC flow-log remediation runbooks, including the Change Manager gated
        change request.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSsmAutomationToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: VpcFlowLogRemediationPermissions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ManageVpcFlowLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:CreateFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeVpcs
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: PassFlowLogDeliveryRoleToFlowLogsService
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:PassRole
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt FlowLogDeliveryRole.Arn
              - Sid: ReadFlowLogDeliveryRoleMetadata
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:GetRole
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt FlowLogDeliveryRole.Arn
              - Sid: RunAndReadFlowLogAutomationDocuments
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:GetDocument
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${FlowLogRemediationDocument}'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${FlowLogChangeRequestDocument}'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${FlowLogChangeTemplate}'
              - Sid: SubmitChangeManagerChangeRequest
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:StartChangeRequestExecution
                  - ssm:CreateChangeRequest
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${FlowLogChangeTemplate}'
              - Sid: ReadAutomationExecutionStatus
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:automation-execution/*'
              - Sid: DescribeAutomationExecutions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-automation-exec-role'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runbook 1: direct remediation. Accepts only a VPC ID, verifies it, is
  # idempotent, and then enables REJECT flow logging to the compliance log group.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FlowLogRemediationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-enable-vpc-flow-logs-reject'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-enable-vpc-flow-logs-reject'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Enables VPC Flow Logs with REJECT traffic capture on the VPC supplied as
          runbook input and delivers them to the compliance CloudWatch Logs log group
          defined by this template. The step is idempotent and the VPC ID is the sole
          source of the target VPC.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC on which reject-traffic flow logging is enabled.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: EnableRejectTrafficFlowLogs
            action: aws:executeScript
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.12
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                VpcId: '{{ VpcId }}'
                LogGroupName: !Ref VpcFlowLogsLogGroup
                DeliverLogsPermissionArn: !GetAtt FlowLogDeliveryRole.Arn
              Script: |
                import boto3
                from botocore.exceptions import ClientError


                def handler(event, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client("ec2")

                    vpc_id = event["VpcId"]
                    log_group_name = event["LogGroupName"]
                    deliver_logs_permission_arn = event["DeliverLogsPermissionArn"]

                    try:
                        vpcs = ec2.describe_vpcs(VpcIds=[vpc_id]).get("Vpcs", [])
                    except ClientError as error:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Unable to describe VPC " + vpc_id + ": " + str(error)
                        )

                    if not vpcs:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "VPC " + vpc_id + " was not found in this account and Region."
                        )

                    try:
                        existing = ec2.describe_flow_logs(
                            Filters=[
                                {"Name": "resource-id", "Values": [vpc_id]},
                                {"Name": "traffic-type", "Values": ["REJECT"]},
                                {"Name": "log-destination-type", "Values": ["cloud-watch-logs"]},
                            ]
                        ).get("FlowLogs", [])
                    except ClientError as error:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Unable to describe existing flow logs for "
                            + vpc_id
                            + ": "
                            + str(error)
                        )

                    for flow_log in existing:
                        if (
                            flow_log.get("LogGroupName") == log_group_name
                            and flow_log.get("FlowLogStatus") != "FAILED"
                        ):
                            return {
                                "FlowLogId": flow_log.get("FlowLogId", ""),
                                "VpcId": vpc_id,
                                "Status": "ALREADY_ENABLED",
                            }

                    try:
                        response = ec2.create_flow_logs(
                            ResourceIds=[vpc_id],
                            ResourceType="VPC",
                            TrafficType="REJECT",
                            LogDestinationType="cloud-watch-logs",
                            LogGroupName=log_group_name,
                            DeliverLogsPermissionArn=deliver_logs_permission_arn,
                        )
                    except ClientError as error:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Unable to create a REJECT flow log for "
                            + vpc_id
                            + ": "
                            + str(error)
                        )

                    unsuccessful = response.get("Unsuccessful", [])
                    if unsuccessful:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "CreateFlowLogs reported unsuccessful results: " + str(unsuccessful)
                        )

                    flow_log_ids = response.get("FlowLogIds", [])
                    if not flow_log_ids:
                        raise RuntimeError("CreateFlowLogs returned no flow log identifier.")

                    return {
                        "FlowLogId": flow_log_ids[0],
                        "VpcId": vpc_id,
                        "Status": "ENABLED",
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: FlowLogId
                Selector: $.Payload.FlowLogId
                Type: String
              - Name: VpcId
                Selector: $.Payload.VpcId
                Type: String
              - Name: Status
                Selector: $.Payload.Status
                Type: String

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Change Manager change template used to gate the remediation. It is defined in
  # this template (no external template name or ARN is assumed) and reuses the
  # runbook above as its executable runbook.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FlowLogChangeTemplate:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-vpc-flow-logs-change-template'
      DocumentType: Automation.ChangeTemplate
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-vpc-flow-logs-change-template'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '1.0'
        description: >-
          Change Manager change template that gates CIS VPC flow-log (REJECT)
          remediation behind a formal change request. It reuses the remediation
          runbook created by this template so no remediation logic is duplicated.
        templateInformation:
          title: !Sub '${NamePrefix} - enable VPC flow logs with reject traffic'
          description: >-
            Approves and then runs the CIS AWS Foundations VPC flow-logging
            remediation for a single VPC.
          categories:
            - Other
        runtimeParameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC that receives reject-traffic flow logging.
            default: ''
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
        executableRunBooks:
          - name: !Ref FlowLogRemediationDocument
            version: '1'
            parameters:
              VpcId:
                - '{{ VpcId }}'
              AutomationAssumeRole:
                - '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runbook 2: change-managed remediation. It makes no EC2 flow-log API call
  # itself; it submits the request through Change Manager, whose approved change
  # request runs the same remediation runbook defined above.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FlowLogChangeRequestDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    DependsOn: FlowLogRemediationDocument
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-request-vpc-flow-logs-change'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-request-vpc-flow-logs-change'
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: !Ref ComplianceTag
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Routes the CIS VPC flow-log (REJECT) remediation request through AWS
          Systems Manager Change Manager as a formal change request. Creating the
          change request performs no EC2 flow-log API call; the flow log is enabled
          only after approval, at which point Change Manager runs the remediation
          runbook referenced by the change template, so the remediation logic is
          never duplicated.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC on which reject-traffic flow logging is requested.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: SubmitFlowLogChangeRequest
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Service: ssm
              Api: StartChangeRequestExecution
              DocumentName: !Ref FlowLogChangeTemplate
              ChangeRequestName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-flowlog-{{ VpcId }}'
              AutoApprove: false
              Parameters:
                VpcId:
                  - '{{ VpcId }}'
                AutomationAssumeRole:
                  - '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: AutomationExecutionId
                Selector: $.AutomationExecutionId
                Type: String
              - Name: ChangeRequestName
                Selector: $.ChangeRequestName
                Type: String

Outputs:

  VpcFlowLogsLogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives VPC flow log data.
    Value: !Ref VpcFlowLogsLogGroup

  VpcFlowLogsLogGroupArn:
    Description: ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives VPC flow log data.
    Value: !GetAtt VpcFlowLogsLogGroup.Arn

  VpcFlowLogsKmsKeyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer managed KMS key that encrypts the flow log data.
    Value: !GetAtt VpcFlowLogsKey.Arn

  FlowLogDeliveryRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role assumed by the VPC Flow Logs delivery service.
    Value: !GetAtt FlowLogDeliveryRole.Arn

  AutomationExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the IAM role supplied as the AutomationAssumeRole runbook input; any
      principal that starts the runbooks needs iam:PassRole for this role.
    Value: !GetAtt AutomationExecutionRole.Arn

  RemediationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation runbook that enables REJECT flow logging directly.
    Value: !Ref FlowLogRemediationDocument

  ChangeRequestDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Automation runbook that submits the flow log change through Change Manager.
    Value: !Ref FlowLogChangeRequestDocument

  ChangeTemplateDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the Change Manager change template document used by the change request runbook.
    Value: !Ref FlowLogChangeTemplate

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Serverless WebSocket API built with API Gateway (WebSocket protocol) that
  asynchronously starts a Step Functions Standard state machine for every
  message received on the $default route. The state machine waits five seconds
  and then posts a response back to the connected client through the API
  Gateway Management API.

Parameters:
  StageName:
    Type: String
    Default: api
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Must be 1-64 characters - letters, numbers, hyphen or underscore.'
    Description: 'Name of the API Gateway stage, also used in the Management API callback endpoint.'

Resources:

  WebSocketApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-websocket-api'
      Description: 'WebSocket API that forwards every unmatched message to a Step Functions state machine.'
      ProtocolType: WEBSOCKET
      RouteSelectionExpression: '$request.body.action'

  ApiGatewayStepFunctionsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: 'Role assumed by API Gateway to start the Step Functions execution.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: apigateway.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: 'StartStateMachineExecution'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - states:StartExecution
                Resource: !Ref StateMachine

  StartExecutionIntegration:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Integration
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      IntegrationType: AWS
      IntegrationMethod: POST
      IntegrationUri: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:states:action/StartExecution'
      CredentialsArn: !GetAtt ApiGatewayStepFunctionsRole.Arn
      RequestTemplates:
        application/json: !Sub |
          {
            "stateMachineArn": "${StateMachine}",
            "input": "{\"connectionId\": \"$context.connectionId\", \"message\": \"$util.escapeJavaScript($input.body)\"}"
          }

  DefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      RouteKey: '$default'
      Target: !Sub 'integrations/${StartExecutionIntegration}'

  Deployment:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Deployment
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      Description: 'Deployment of the WebSocket API routes.'

  Stage:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Stage
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      StageName: !Ref StageName
      AutoDeploy: true
      DeploymentId: !Ref Deployment
      Description: 'WebSocket API stage used by the Management API callback endpoint.'

  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: 'Role assumed by the state machine to post messages back to WebSocket connections.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: 'ManageWebSocketConnections'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - execute-api:ManageConnections
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:execute-api:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${WebSocketApi}/${StageName}/POST/@connections/*'

  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-websocket'
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      Definition:
        Comment: 'Waits five seconds after a WebSocket message and posts a response back to the connection.'
        StartAt: Initialize
        States:
          Initialize:
            Type: Pass
            Parameters:
              connectionId.$: $.connectionId
              message.$: $.message
            Next: WaitForResponse
          WaitForResponse:
            Type: Wait
            Seconds: 5
            Next: PostToConnection
          PostToConnection:
            Type: Task
            Resource: 'arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:apigatewaymanagementapi:postToConnection'
            Parameters:
              ApiEndpoint: !Sub 'https://${WebSocketApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${StageName}'
              ConnectionId.$: $.connectionId
              Data.$: 'States.Base64Encode($.message)'
            End: true

Outputs:
  WebSocketUrl:
    Description: 'WebSocket (WSS) URL clients use to connect to the API.'
    Value: !Sub 'wss://${WebSocketApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${StageName}'
  ApiId:
    Description: 'ID of the WebSocket API.'
    Value: !Ref WebSocketApi
  StageName:
    Description: 'Name of the deployed API Gateway stage.'
    Value: !Ref StageName

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Automated, self-contained EC2 Image Builder pipeline that produces a CIS Level 1 hardened,
  Elastic Beanstalk-ready Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 (Graviton) AMI. The stack creates its own VPC,
  private build subnet, route table, builder and endpoint security groups, S3 build-log bucket,
  SNS notification topic, customer-managed KMS key, S3/SSM VPC endpoints, IAM roles and instance
  profile, a custom Elastic Beanstalk compatibility component, a vulnerability scan component, the
  image recipe, build infrastructure, distribution configuration, a daily build pipeline and a
  180-day AMI lifecycle policy.

# OBJECTIVE COMMENT (vulnerability scanning): Vulnerability scanning is not exposed as a property of
# AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe, AWS::ImageBuilder::ImagePipeline or their test configuration, so it is
# implemented here with a dedicated test-phase Image Builder component (VulnerabilityScanComponent) that
# runs the package security-advisory scanner inside the build instance before distribution. A native
# Amazon Inspector based scanning resource type would have to be confirmed against the CloudFormation
# registry before it could be added to this template, therefore it is intentionally omitted rather than
# invented. Add it only after registry confirmation.
#
# OBJECTIVE COMMENT (private, endpoint-based egress): The build subnet is private (no public IP mapping,
# no internet gateway, no 0.0.0.0/0 route) and the builder security group only permits egress to the VPC
# CIDR. All AWS-service traffic - Amazon S3 for components and build logs, AWS Systems Manager for the
# Image Builder control channel - is routed through the S3 gateway endpoint and the ssm / ssmmessages /
# ec2messages interface endpoints created in this template, and DNS resolution uses the VPC resolver at
# the VPC CIDR .2 address. Any AL2023 OS package that resolves to a public internet address will not
# traverse the build subnet; if direct OS-repository internet access is strictly required it must be
# satisfied through an S3-backed package mirror reachable via the S3 gateway endpoint rather than by
# re-introducing a 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 security-group rule.
#
# NOTE: No EC2 key pair is created or referenced anywhere - Image Builder connects to the build instance
# through AWS Systems Manager (AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore + EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder) using the
# instance profile created below, which is the secure, keyless connection method.

Parameters:

  OrganizationId:
    Type: String
    Default: o-abcdefghij
    AllowedPattern: '^o-[a-z0-9]{10,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an AWS Organizations ID such as o-abcdefghij.
    Description: >-
      AWS Organizations ID whose member accounts may launch the produced AMI
      (used to build the launch permission organization ARN).

  DevAccountId:
    Type: String
    Default: '111111111111'
    AllowedPattern: '^\d{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a 12-digit AWS account ID.
    Description: AWS account ID of the development deployment environment that the AMI is shared with.

  ProdAccountId:
    Type: String
    Default: '222222222222'
    AllowedPattern: '^\d{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a 12-digit AWS account ID.
    Description: AWS account ID of the production deployment environment that the AMI is shared with.

  ParentImageName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'cis-hardened-image-level-1-on-amazon-linux-2023-arm-r5sqt5uxgygqi/x.x.x'
    Description: >-
      Name/version of the CIS Level 1 hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 parent image used by the recipe.
      This image is an external artifact (AWS Machine Image / Marketplace subscription) that must be
      resolvable in this account and region; the recipe resolves it to the current region and partition.
      Override this value if your CIS hardened image name, version or region differs.

Resources:

  ##########################################################################
  # Customer-managed KMS key for the build-log bucket and the notification topic
  ##########################################################################

  BuildLogsKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: Customer-managed key for Image Builder build logs and pipeline notifications
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableRootAccountPermissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowSnsToUseKeyForTopicEncryption
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: sns.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-kms'

  ##########################################################################
  # Networking - private build subnet with VPC endpoint based egress
  ##########################################################################

  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.255.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-vpc'

  BuildSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: 10.255.0.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-build-subnet'

  BuildRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-build-rt'

  BuildSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref BuildSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref BuildRouteTable

  BuilderSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Egress scoped to the VPC for the Image Builder build and test instances
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: 10.255.0.0/16
          Description: HTTPS to VPC endpoints, the VPC DNS resolver and services inside the VPC
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 10.255.0.0/16
          Description: HTTP to services inside the VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-builder-sg'

  EndpointSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: HTTPS access from the build subnet to the VPC interface endpoints
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: 10.255.0.0/16

  ##########################################################################
  # Image Builder build log bucket
  ##########################################################################

  LogBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt BuildLogsKmsKey.Arn
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-logs'

  LogBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref LogBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyInsecureConnections
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt LogBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${LogBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                aws:SecureTransport: 'false'
          - Sid: AllowImageBuilderBuildLogAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS:
                - !GetAtt ImageBuilderInstanceRole.Arn
                - !GetAtt ImageBuilderServiceRole.Arn
            Action:
              - s3:AbortMultipartUpload
              - s3:GetBucketLocation
              - s3:GetObject
              - s3:ListBucket
              - s3:PutObject
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt LogBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${LogBucket.Arn}/*'

  ##########################################################################
  # SNS topic for pipeline failure notifications (encrypted with the CMK)
  ##########################################################################

  BuildNotificationTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
    Properties:
      TopicName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-notifications'
      DisplayName: Image Builder pipeline notifications
      KmsMasterKeyId: !GetAtt BuildLogsKmsKey.Arn

  ##########################################################################
  # IAM - instance role/profile for build and test instances
  ##########################################################################

  ImageBuilderInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Role assumed by the EC2 Image Builder build and test instances
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilderECRContainerBuilds'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ImageBuilderBuildLogBucketAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: BuildLogObjects
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:AbortMultipartUpload
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                Resource: !Sub '${LogBucket.Arn}/*'
              - Sid: BuildLogBucketMetadata
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetBucketLocation
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Resource: !GetAtt LogBucket.Arn
              - Sid: UseCustomerManagedKeyForBuildLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:GenerateDataKey
                  - kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext
                  - kms:DescribeKey
                Resource: !GetAtt BuildLogsKmsKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-imagebuilder-instance-role'

  ImageBuilderInstanceProfile:
    Type: AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile
    Properties:
      Roles:

  ##########################################################################
  # IAM - Image Builder service execution role (pipeline + lifecycle policy)

  ImageBuilderServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

      Description: Execution role for the EC2 Image Builder pipeline and AMI lifecycle policy
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:

        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: imagebuilder.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ImageBuilderServiceAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ImageBuilderAll
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - imagebuilder:*
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: Ec2ImageAndSnapshotActions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:CreateImage
                  - ec2:CopyImage
                  - ec2:CreateSnapshot
                  - ec2:DeleteSnapshot
                  - ec2:DescribeSnapshots
                  - ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute
                  - ec2:DescribeImageAttribute
                  - ec2:ModifyImageAttribute
                  - ec2:DescribeImages
                  - ec2:EnableImageDeprecation
                  - ec2:DisableImageDeprecation
                  - ec2:CreateTags
                  - ec2:DescribeInstances
                  - ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus
                  - ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes
                  - ec2:DescribeSubnets
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplates
                  - ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions
                  - ec2:GetEbsEncryptionByDefault
                  - ec2:RunInstances
                  - ec2:StopInstances
                  - ec2:TerminateInstances

              - Sid: SystemsManager

                  - ssm:GetParameter
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                  - ssm:ListCommandInvocations
                  - ssm:ListCommands
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogs
                Effect: Allow

                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: BuildLogBucket
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetBucketLocation
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:ListBucket

                Effect: Allow

  ##########################################################################
  # Image Builder components
  ##########################################################################

  ElasticBeanstalkCompatibilityComponent:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::Component
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-eb-al2023-arm-compat'
      Description: Pre-configures Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 for Elastic Beanstalk compatibility
      Platform: Linux
      SupportedOsVersions:
        - 'Amazon Linux 2023'
      Version: '1.0.0'
      ChangeDescription: Initial version
      Data: |
        name: ElasticBeanstalkAL2023Compat
        description: Pre-configures Amazon Linux 2023 for Elastic Beanstalk compatibility.
        schemaVersion: 1.0
        phases:
          - name: build
            steps:
              - name: InstallElasticBeanstalkHostDependencies
                action: ExecuteBash
                inputs:
                  commands:
                    - set -euxo pipefail
                    - dnf -y install python3 python3-pip git gcc make httpd nginx logrotate
                    - dnf -y install amazon-ssm-agent
                    - systemctl enable amazon-ssm-agent
              - name: CreateElasticBeanstalkDirectoryLayout
                action: ExecuteBash
                inputs:
                  commands:
                    - set -euxo pipefail
                    - install -d -m 0755 /opt/elasticbeanstalk
                    - install -d -m 0755 /opt/elasticbeanstalk/bin
                    - install -d -m 0755 /opt/elasticbeanstalk/hooks
                    - install -d -m 0755 /opt/elasticbeanstalk/deployment
                    - install -d -m 0755 /var/log/elasticbeanstalk
                    - install -d -m 0755 /var/log/httpd
                    - install -d -m 0755 /var/log/nginx
                    - install -d -m 0755 /etc/httpd/conf.d
                    - install -d -m 0755 /etc/nginx/conf.d
              - name: ConfigureElasticBeanstalkLogRotation
                action: ExecuteBash
                inputs:
                  commands:
                    - |
                      cat > /etc/logrotate.d/elasticbeanstalk <<'LOGROTATE'
                      /var/log/elasticbeanstalk/*.log {
                          daily
                          rotate 7
                          missingok
                          notifempty
                          compress
                          copytruncate
                      }
                      LOGROTATE
                    - |
                      cat > /etc/logrotate.d/beanstalk-web <<'LOGROTATE'
                      /var/log/httpd/*.log /var/log/nginx/*.log {
                          daily
                          rotate 7
                          missingok
                          notifempty
                          compress
                          copytruncate
                      }
                      LOGROTATE
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-eb-al2023-arm-compat'

  VulnerabilityScanComponent:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::Component
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-vulnerability-scan-al2023'
      Description: Scans the Amazon Linux 2023 image under test for applicable security advisories
      Platform: Linux
      SupportedOsVersions:
        - 'Amazon Linux 2023'
      Version: '1.0.0'
      ChangeDescription: Initial version
      Data: |
        name: VulnerabilityScanAL2023
        description: Records the applicable security advisories for the image under test.
        schemaVersion: 1.0
        phases:
          - name: test
            steps:
              - name: ScanForSecurityAdvisories
                action: ExecuteBash
                inputs:
                  commands:
                    - |
                      set -euxo pipefail
                      REPORT=/var/log/imagebuilder-vulnerability-scan.log
                      {
                        echo "EC2 Image Builder vulnerability scan report"
                        echo "Generated: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
                        echo
                        echo "--- Applicable security advisories (dnf updateinfo) ---"
                      } > "${REPORT}"
                      dnf -y makecache >> "${REPORT}" 2>&1 || true
                      if ! dnf updateinfo list security >> "${REPORT}" 2>&1; then
                        echo "dnf updateinfo metadata is unavailable, falling back to a package update check" >> "${REPORT}"
                        dnf check-update >> "${REPORT}" 2>&1 || true
                      fi
                      echo "--- End of vulnerability scan report ---" >> "${REPORT}"
                      cat "${REPORT}"
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-vulnerability-scan-al2023'

  ##########################################################################
  # Image recipe
  # NOTE: image tests are configured on the pipeline (ImageTestsConfiguration), because the
  # AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe resource does not expose a test configuration property.
  ##########################################################################

  ImageRecipe:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-eb-cis-recipe'
      Description: >-
        CIS Level 1 hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 image pre-configured for Elastic Beanstalk
      Version: '1.0.0'
      ParentImage: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:imagebuilder:${AWS::Region}:aws:image/${ParentImageName}'
      Components:
        - ComponentArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:imagebuilder:${AWS::Region}:aws:component/update-linux/x.x.x'
        - ComponentArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:imagebuilder:${AWS::Region}:aws:component/aws-cli-version-2-linux/x.x.x'
        - ComponentArn: !Ref ElasticBeanstalkCompatibilityComponent
        - ComponentArn: !Ref VulnerabilityScanComponent
        - ComponentArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:imagebuilder:${AWS::Region}:aws:component/reboot-linux/x.x.x'
      BlockDeviceMappings:
        - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
          Ebs:
            DeleteOnTermination: true
            Encrypted: true
            VolumeSize: 50
            VolumeType: gp3
      WorkingDirectory: /tmp
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-eb-cis-recipe'

  ##########################################################################
  # Build infrastructure
  ##########################################################################

  BuildInfrastructureConfiguration:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::InfrastructureConfiguration
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-build-infra'
      Description: Build infrastructure for the CIS hardened, Elastic Beanstalk-ready AL2023 ARM64 image
      InstanceProfileName: !Ref ImageBuilderInstanceProfile
      InstanceTypes:
        - t4g.medium
        - m6g.large
      SubnetId: !Ref BuildSubnet
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref BuilderSecurityGroup
      TerminateInstanceOnFailure: true
      SnsTopicArn: !Ref BuildNotificationTopic
      Logging:
        S3Logs:
          S3BucketName: !Ref LogBucket
          S3KeyPrefix: imagebuilder-build-logs
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-build-infra'

  ##########################################################################
  # Distribution configuration
  ##########################################################################

  ImageDistributionConfiguration:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::DistributionConfiguration
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-distribution'
      Description: >-
        Distributes the hardened AL2023 ARM64 AMI in the current region and shares it with the
        organization, the development account and the production account
      Distributions:
        - Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          AmiDistributionConfiguration:
            Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cis-al2023-arm-eb-{{imagebuilder:buildDate}}'
            Description: >-
              CIS Level 1 hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 image pre-configured for Elastic Beanstalk
            AmiTags:
              Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cis-al2023-arm-eb'
              ImageBuilderLifecyclePolicy: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
              Platform: Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64
              Hardening: CIS-Level-1
            LaunchPermissionConfiguration:
              OrganizationArns:
                - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:organizations::${AWS::AccountId}:organization/${OrganizationId}'
              UserIds:
                - !Ref DevAccountId
                - !Ref ProdAccountId
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-distribution'

  ##########################################################################
  # Daily pipeline (01:00 UTC = cron(0 1 * * ? *); the Schedule schema has no Timezone field,
  # so the UTC offset is expressed directly in the cron hour)
  ##########################################################################

  ImagePipeline:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::ImagePipeline
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-eb-pipeline'
      Description: Daily build of the CIS hardened, Elastic Beanstalk-ready Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 AMI
      Status: ENABLED
      ImageRecipeArn: !Ref ImageRecipe
      InfrastructureConfigurationArn: !Ref BuildInfrastructureConfiguration
      DistributionConfigurationArn: !Ref ImageDistributionConfiguration
      ImageTestsConfiguration:
        ImageTestsEnabled: true
        TimeoutMinutes: 60
      Schedule:
        ScheduleExpression: 'cron(0 1 * * ? *)'
        PipelineExecutionStartCondition: EXPRESSION_MATCH_AND_DEPENDENCY_UPDATES_AVAILABLE
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-eb-pipeline'

  ##########################################################################
  # AMI lifecycle policy - delete after 6 months, never remove the newest AMI
  ##########################################################################

  AmiLifecyclePolicy:
    Type: AWS::ImageBuilder::LifecyclePolicy
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-ami-lifecycle'
      Description: >-
        Deletes the AMIs and snapshots produced by this pipeline after 180 days (6 months) while
        always retaining the most recent image, and excludes images tagged for retention
      Status: ENABLED
      ExecutionRole: !GetAtt ImageBuilderServiceRole.Arn
      ResourceType: AMI_IMAGE
      ResourceSelection:
        TagMap:
          ImageBuilderLifecyclePolicy: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
      PolicyDetails:
        - Action:
            Type: DELETE
            IncludeResources:
              Amis: true
              Snapshots: true
          Filter:
            Type: AGE
            Value: 180
            Unit: DAYS
            RetainAtLeast: 1
          ExclusionRules:
            Amis:
              TagMap:
                DoNotDelete: 'true'
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-al2023-arm-ami-lifecycle'

    Description: ARN of the Image Builder pipeline that builds the hardened AL2023 ARM64 AMI daily
    Value: !Ref ImagePipeline

    Description: ARN of the Image Builder image recipe for the hardened AL2023 ARM64 image
    Value: !Ref ImageRecipe

    Value: !Ref BuildNotificationTopic

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Serverless Maths MCP API with Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Cognito authentication.

Parameters:
  DeploymentStage:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    Description: Name of the API Gateway deployment stage.
  UserPoolName:
    Type: String
    Default: maths-mcp-users
    Description: Name of the Cognito User Pool.
  AppClientName:
    Type: String
    Default: maths-mcp-client
    Description: Name of the Cognito User Pool Client.

Resources:

  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-maths-mcp-lambda-role'
      Description: Execution role for the Maths MCP Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  MathsMcpFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-maths-mcp'
      Description: Placeholder Maths MCP serverless handler, updated later.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 512
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json

          def handler(event, context):
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "headers": {
                      "Content-Type": "application/json",
                      "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*"
                  },
                  "body": json.dumps({
                      "status": "ok",
                      "service": "maths-mcp",
                      "version": "0.0.1"
                  })
              }

  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Ref UserPoolName
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email
      UsernameConfiguration:
        CaseSensitive: false
      Policies:
        PasswordPolicy:
          MinimumLength: 8
          RequireUppercase: true
          RequireLowercase: true
          RequireNumbers: true
          RequireSymbols: false

  UserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Ref AppClientName
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
      AccessTokenValidity: 1
      IdTokenValidity: 1
      RefreshTokenValidity: 30
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: hours
        IdToken: hours
        RefreshToken: days

  RestApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-maths-mcp-api'
      Description: Serverless Maths MCP API.
      EndpointConfiguration:
        Types:
          - REGIONAL

  CognitoAuthorizer:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Authorizer
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-maths-mcp-cognito-authorizer'
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      Type: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      ProviderARNs:
        - !GetAtt UserPool.Arn
      IdentitySource: method.request.header.Authorization

  McpResource:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Resource
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ParentId: !GetAtt RestApi.RootResourceId
      PathPart: mcp

  McpPostMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ResourceId: !Ref McpResource
      HttpMethod: POST
      AuthorizationType: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      AuthorizerId: !Ref CognitoAuthorizer
      ApiKeyRequired: false
      Integration:
        Type: AWS_PROXY
        IntegrationHttpMethod: POST
        Uri: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${MathsMcpFunction.Arn}/invocations'

  McpOptionsMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ResourceId: !Ref McpResource
      HttpMethod: OPTIONS
      AuthorizationType: NONE
      ApiKeyRequired: false
      Integration:
        Type: MOCK
        RequestTemplates:
          application/json: '{"statusCode": 200}'
        IntegrationResponses:
          - StatusCode: '200'
            ResponseParameters:
              method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Origin: "'*'"
              method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: "'OPTIONS,POST'"
              method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: "'Content-Type,Authorization,X-Amz-Date,X-Api-Key,X-Amz-Security-Token'"
            ResponseTemplates:
              application/json: ''
      MethodResponses:
        - StatusCode: '200'
          ResponseParameters:
            method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Origin: true
            method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: true
            method.response.header.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: true

  RootGetMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ResourceId: !GetAtt RestApi.RootResourceId
      HttpMethod: GET
      AuthorizationType: NONE
      ApiKeyRequired: false
      Integration:
        Type: AWS_PROXY
        IntegrationHttpMethod: POST
        Uri: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${MathsMcpFunction.Arn}/invocations'

  ApiDeployment:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Deployment
    DependsOn:
      - McpPostMethod
      - McpOptionsMethod
      - RootGetMethod
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      Description: Deployment for the Maths MCP API.

  ApiStage:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Stage
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      DeploymentId: !Ref ApiDeployment
      StageName: !Ref DeploymentStage
      Description: Stage for the Maths MCP API.

  LambdaApiGatewayPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    DependsOn:
      - ApiStage
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref MathsMcpFunction
      Principal: apigateway.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:execute-api:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RestApi}/*/*'

Outputs:
  ApiEndpointUrl:
    Description: Base URL of the deployed Maths MCP API stage.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${RestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${DeploymentStage}'
  McpEndpointUrl:
    Description: Authenticated MCP POST endpoint URL.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${RestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${DeploymentStage}/mcp'
  HealthCheckUrl:
    Description: Public health check endpoint URL.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${RestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${DeploymentStage}/'
  UserPoolId:
    Description: Cognito User Pool ID.
    Value: !Ref UserPool
  UserPoolClientId:
    Description: Cognito User Pool Client ID.
    Value: !Ref UserPoolClient
  AuthorizerId:
    Description: API Gateway Cognito authorizer ID.
    Value: !Ref CognitoAuthorizer
  LambdaFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the Maths MCP Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref MathsMcpFunction

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Self-contained RAPIDS AI development environment on Amazon SageMaker. Creates a
  dedicated VPC with a public subnet (holding a NAT gateway) and a private subnet
  for the notebook, an egress-restricted security group, an Amazon SageMaker
  execution role, a customer managed KMS key encrypting the 50 GB notebook
  volume, a SageMaker code repository for https://github.com/rapidsai/notebooks,
  an S3 gateway VPC endpoint, a base64-encoded lifecycle configuration that
  installs a RAPIDS conda environment and registers a Jupyter kernel on both
  create and start, and an ml.t3.medium notebook instance named "rapidsai".

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Networking: dedicated VPC. A public subnet carries the NAT gateway; a
  # private subnet hosts the notebook, which gains outbound connectivity through
  # the NAT gateway and an S3 gateway endpoint.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAPIDSVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-vpc

  RAPIDSInternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-igw

  RAPIDSGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref RAPIDSInternetGateway

  # Public subnet: no automatic public IP assignment. Hosts the NAT gateway.
  RAPIDSPublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone:
        Fn::Select:
          - 0
          - Fn::GetAZs: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-public-subnet

  # Private subnet: hosts the notebook instance, IGW-less, egress via NAT.
  RAPIDSPrivateSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone:
        Fn::Select:
          - 0
          - Fn::GetAZs: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-private-subnet

  RAPIDSPublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-public-rt

  RAPIDSPublicDefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    # The route can only be created after the internet gateway is attached to the
    # VPC; a Ref/GetAtt on the gateway alone does not express that ordering.
    DependsOn: RAPIDSGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref RAPIDSPublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref RAPIDSInternetGateway

  RAPIDSPublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref RAPIDSPublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref RAPIDSPublicRouteTable

  # NAT gateway providing scoped internet egress for the private subnet.
  RAPIDSNatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-nat-eip

  RAPIDSNatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    DependsOn: RAPIDSPublicDefaultRoute
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt RAPIDSNatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref RAPIDSPublicSubnet
      ConnectivityType: public
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-nat-gateway

  RAPIDSPrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-private-rt

  RAPIDSPrivateDefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref RAPIDSPrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref RAPIDSNatGateway

  RAPIDSPrivateSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref RAPIDSPrivateSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref RAPIDSPrivateRouteTable

  # S3 gateway endpoint so AWS service access stays on the AWS network and inside
  # the VPC routing domain.
  RAPIDSS3GatewayEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds:
        - !Ref RAPIDSPrivateRouteTable
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowRapidsNotebookS3Access
            Effect: Allow
            Principal: '*'
            Action:
              - s3:GetObject
              - s3:GetObjectVersion
              - s3:PutObject
              - s3:ListBucket
              - s3:GetBucketLocation
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::rapidsai-*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::rapidsai-*/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Security group for the notebook instance: egress scoped to the VPC CIDR
  # (which covers the NAT gateway and the S3 endpoint path), no ingress.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAPIDSNotebookSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Egress-scoped security group for the RAPIDS AI SageMaker notebook instance
      VpcId: !Ref RAPIDSVpc
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: HTTPS within the VPC (NAT gateway and endpoint path)
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: HTTP within the VPC (NAT gateway and endpoint path)
        - IpProtocol: udp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: DNS resolution within the VPC
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16
          Description: DNS resolution over TCP within the VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-notebook-sg

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SageMaker execution role.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SageMakerExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the RAPIDS AI SageMaker notebook instance
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSageMakerServiceToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: sagemaker.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSageMakerFullAccess
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-sagemaker-notebook-role

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Customer managed key that encrypts the notebook's 50 GB EBS volume. The key
  # policy grants usage to the SageMaker execution role.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAPIDSKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: Customer managed key encrypting the RAPIDS AI SageMaker notebook volume
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Id: rapidsai-notebook-key-policy
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowSageMakerNotebookRoleToUseKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !GetAtt SageMakerExecutionRole.Arn
            Action:
              - kms:DescribeKey
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:ReEncryptFrom
              - kms:ReEncryptTo
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext
              - kms:CreateGrant
              - kms:ListGrants
              - kms:RevokeGrant
            Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: rapidsai-notebook-key

  RAPIDSKmsKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/rapidsai-notebook
      TargetKeyId: !Ref RAPIDSKmsKey

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Least-privilege inline policy attached to the SageMaker execution role.
  # Defined as a standalone AWS::IAM::Policy so that the KMS key ARN can be
  # referenced without creating a circular dependency with the key policy.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SageMakerNotebookAccessPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: rapidsai-notebook-access
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerExecutionRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: NotebookVolumeEncryptionKeyAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - kms:DescribeKey
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:ReEncryptFrom
              - kms:ReEncryptTo
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext
              - kms:CreateGrant
              - kms:ListGrants
              - kms:RevokeGrant
            Resource: !GetAtt RAPIDSKmsKey.Arn
          - Sid: RapidsSampleAndArtifactS3Access
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:GetObject
              - s3:GetObjectVersion
              - s3:PutObject
              - s3:ListBucket
              - s3:GetBucketLocation
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::rapidsai-*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::rapidsai-*/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Code repository cloned automatically into the notebook. A notebook instance
  # cannot reference a raw Git URL, it must reference a CodeRepository.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAPIDSCodeRepository:
    Type: AWS::SageMaker::CodeRepository
    Properties:
      CodeRepositoryName: rapidsai-notebooks
      GitConfig:
        RepositoryUrl: https://github.com/rapidsai/notebooks
        Branch: main

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lifecycle configuration. Renaming this resource forces replacement of the
  # notebook instance, and the name is kept well below the 63 character limit.
  # Both scripts run as ec2-user, create/activate the RAPIDS conda environment
  # and register a Jupyter kernel. They are guarded so restarts are idempotent.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAPIDSNotebookLifecycleConfig:
    Type: AWS::SageMaker::NotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig
    Properties:
      NotebookInstanceLifecycleConfigName: rapidsai-lifecycle-config
      OnCreate:
        - Content: !Base64 |
            #!/bin/bash
            set -e
            sudo -u ec2-user -i <<'RAPIDS_SETUP'
            set -e
            source /home/ec2-user/anaconda3/bin/activate
            if ! conda env list | grep -qE '^rapids[[:space:]]'; then
              conda create --yes --name rapids \
                --channel rapidsai --channel conda-forge --channel nvidia \
                rapids=latest python=3.11 cudatoolkit=11.8 ipykernel
            fi
            source /home/ec2-user/anaconda3/bin/activate rapids
            if ! jupyter kernelspec list 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'rapids'; then

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
